subject: Discovery recap — tool calling & structured output requirements
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference.com>
To: Anna Torres <anna@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Jul 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap — tool calling & structured output requirements

Hi Anna — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and next steps so we’re aligned. Please reply with any corrections.

Summary of pain points you described:
- Current conversational workflow occasionally returns inconsistent JSON payloads from the agent layer, causing downstream processing errors (order ingestion failures ~3–5% of chats).
- Your data pipeline requires deterministic formatting for SKU updates; any extra text or missing fields needs manual fixes.
- Latency spikes during peak traffic (holiday promos) are forcing you to throttle features.

Current stack / constraints:
- Front end: React storefront + serverless API gateway (AWS).
- Orchestration: Microservices in ECS/Fargate; you run a mix of CPU workers and a smaller GPU inference fleet for heavy models.
- Strict QA requirement: JSON payloads consumed by the fulfillment pipeline must match the schema exactly; no free-text wrappers around required fields.

Success criteria you mentioned:
1) Deterministic structured output: agent must return valid JSON matching a predefined schema 99.9% of the time in production.
2) Function/tool calling: ability to call a backend function with sanitized params (intent, sku_list, quantity_map) with no ambiguity.
3) Latency SLO: p95 token generation latency under 250ms for the critical path.
4) Operational: slot for canary rollouts and automatic fallback to smaller quantized model under load.

What we discussed (technical):
- We recommend using Redwood's tool-calling primitives to enforce structured output plus a JSON schema validator at the runtime boundary.
- Example approach: agent produces a single JSON object (no surrounding commentary). For retries, Redwood can return a "structured_response" token and raw model output in parallel for audit.
- We can surface deterministic formatting success metrics in Console (per-prompt schema pass rate).

Attached: discovery-notes.pdf (call transcript + checklist), example-json-schema.json (proto schema we sketched during call).

Proposed next steps:
1) You confirm the attached schema or provide a canonical schema file.
2) We spin up a 2-week POC: sample traffic replay with schema validation, tool-calling integration, and dashboarding.
3) Schedule a technical walkthrough with your infra team (Dev + SRE) to map endpoints and throttling behavior.

Would Wednesday (Jul 28) at 9am PT for a 30m tech deep-dive work for you? I’ll include Dev and Marissa.

Thanks again — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachment: example-json-schema.json (JSON, 4KB)

From: Anna Torres <anna@acme-retail.com>

Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acme-retail.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Jul 2026 09:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — tool calling & structured output requirements

Thanks Jordan — this looks right and captures the call well. A few clarifications / asks from our side: 

- Schema: Confirming we need a single top-level object with fields: order_id (string), items (array of {sku:string, qty:int}), billing (object), shipping (object), and optional metadata. We’ll send your team the canonical schema file (should be with exact types).
- Determinism target: We can accept 99.5% schema-valid output for the POC, with a plan to reach 99.9% before GA.
- Latency: 250ms p95 is what we need for the critical checkout flow. If Redwood can demonstrate consistent hits <250ms p95 in the POC environment, that’s a green light.

Procurement is looped in to start paperwork after we validate the technical approach. Their timeline: initial T&Cs review ~1 week, vendor security questionnaire (SOC2) within 2 weeks.

Yes — Wed Jul 28 at 9am PT works for a 30m tech walkthrough. Please send a calendar invite and any pre-read for our SREs.

A couple more items we’ll need for the POC:
- Example of how Redwood’s runtime surfaces schema pass/fail metrics (dashboard screenshot or link).
- Sample error payloads (what data is returned when the schema fails).

Thanks — Anna
Anna Torres
Head of AI Platforms | Acme Retail
anna@acme-retail.com

Great — thanks for confirming, Anna. Calendar invite sent for Wed 9:00–9:30am PT with a short pre-read. I’ve looped in Marissa (Customer Success) and Dev (Solutions) to lead the tech walkthrough.

Quick answers to your asks and POC plan: 
- Dashboard: attaching redwood-sla-summary.pdf which includes example Console views for schema pass rate, per-prompt validation, and latency heatmaps. We’ll also create a temporary dashboard for the POC workspace so you can watch schema pass-rate in real time.
- Error payloads: during the POC we’ll return both the raw model output and a normalized error object when validation fails: {"error_type":"schema_mismatch","field_errors":[...],"raw_output":"..."} — this is for visibility and audit. We’ll keep raw_output confined to your private workspace for compliance.

POC timeline (proposed):
1) Week 0: exchange canonical schema file and sample traffic (anonymized).
2) Week 1: Redwood config + run sample replay; initial schema pass metrics collected.
3) Week 2: tuning and rules (prompt engineering, deterministic instruction sets, fallback policy).
4) Review & decision meeting end of Week 2.

Security & procurement: we have SOC2 evidence ready; I’ll route the link to Procurement and your security contact post-call.

Next immediate ask for your team: please share the canonical schema file and a small sample of anonymized chat payloads (50–200 records) so Dev can do an initial offline validation before Wed. You can upload to the Drive link in the invite or email to me directly.

Attaching: redwood-sla-summary.pdf (5 pages).

Thanks — Jordan
